title: Fix it: format a list of names
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You have a list of names that is formatted as a single string with a pipe separator. The names have extra spaces and are in different cases. Clean them up: trim the spaces, convert to title case (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase), and return them as a newline-separated string.

Title case formula: take the first character, uppercase it, concatenate the rest of the string in lowercase. In DataWeave, a string is an array: `s[0]` is the first character and `s[1 to -1]` is the rest.

For the sample, input `" alice | BOB | Carol "` should produce `Alice\nBob\nCarol`.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output text/plain
---
payload splitBy "|" map (upper($[0]) ++ lower($[1 to -1])) joinBy "\n"
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
forgets to trim, so spaces stay in the names
solution:
%dw 2.0
output text/plain
---
payload splitBy "|" map (do { var n = trim($) --- upper(n[0]) ++ lower(n[1 to -1]) }) joinBy "\n"

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output text/plain
---
payload splitBy "|" map (upper($[0]) ++ lower($[1 to -1])) joinBy "\n"

explanation.approach: Three chained operations: split on the separator, transform each element, join with the output separator. The trap is remembering that splitBy keeps the spaces in each name — each element needs trimming before capitalization.

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output text/plain
---
payload splitBy "|" map (do { var n = trim($) --- upper(n[0]) ++ lower(n[1 to -1]) }) joinBy "\n"
snippets.note: splitBy breaks on pipes; map transforms each (trim first, then build title case: first letter uppercase, rest lowercase); joinBy reassembles with newlines. The `do { var n = ... }` inside map lets you name the trimmed string so you can split it.

snippets.label: What splitBy actually produces
snippets.note: The spaces are still there. Each element keeps its surrounding whitespace. Without trim(), the first character of " alice " would be processed, which is a space.

snippets.label: The wrong way: forgetting to trim
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output text/plain
---
payload splitBy "|" map (upper($[0]) ++ lower($[1 to -1])) joinBy "\n"
snippets.note: Without trim(), each name still has its spaces. When you apply the formula to " alice ", the first char is a space and the rest is "alice ", so you get space + lowercase(alice ), which gives " alice ". The spaces are untouched.

snippets.label: String slicing: characters as array indices
snippets.note: [0] gets the first character, [1 to -1] gets from index 1 to the last. So for a string `n`, the formula is always upper(n[0]) ++ lower(n[1 to -1]).

snippets.label: trim() behavior
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{untrimmed: " hello ", trimmed: trim(" hello ")}
snippets.note: trim() removes whitespace from both ends. It does not affect spaces inside the word.

snippets.label: The pipe separator behavior
snippets.note: The pipe is literal, not regex. A pipe is just a character, so `splitBy "|"` means 'split on this exact string'.

snippets.label: joinBy assembles back
snippets.note: The newline literal `\n` produces actual newlines in the output, not the characters backslash and n.
